name: Flemish Beef Stew (Stoofvlees)
description: Slow-braised beef in dark Belgian beer with onions, mustard and gingerbread. Classic with fries.
ingredients: 1 kg beef stewing meat, in large cubes
steps: Pat the beef dry, season and dust with flour. Brown in batches in butter in a heavy casserole; set aside.
Soften the onions in the same pan for 10 minutes, then return the meat.
Add the beer, crumbled stock cube, bay leaves, thyme, sugar and vinegar. Spread the mustard on the gingerbread and lay it on top.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat falls apart.
Season to taste and serve with fries and mayonnaise.

name: Belgian Endive Gratin with Ham
description: Witloof in hesp: braised endives wrapped in ham, baked under a cheesy béchamel. Served with mashed potatoes.
steps: Remove the bitter core of the endives and braise them in a covered pan with a knob of butter for 20 minutes. Drain well.
Boil the potatoes and mash with a little milk and butter.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk. Stir in two thirds of the cheese and season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Wrap each endive in a slice of ham, place in an oven dish, cover with the sauce and the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Serve with the mash.

name: Vol-au-Vent
description: Chicken, mushrooms and meatballs in a creamy sauce, served in puff pastry shells or with fries.
steps: Poach the chicken with carrots, onion, celery and stock cube in water for 1 hour. Lift out, pull the meat from the bones and strain 800 ml of the stock.
Poach the small meatballs in the stock for 5 minutes. Fry the mushrooms in a little butter.
Make a roux with butter and flour, whisk in the warm stock and simmer until thick. Add cream and lemon juice.
Fold in the chicken, meatballs and mushrooms. Season and serve in warmed puff pastry shells.

name: Carrot Stoemp with Sausages
description: Rustic Brussels mash of potatoes and carrots with pan-fried pork sausages.
steps: Boil potatoes and carrots together in salted water for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the onion in a little butter and fry the sausages until cooked through.
Drain the vegetables and mash coarsely with butter, warm milk, onion and nutmeg. Season and serve with the sausages.

name: Spinach Stoemp with Fried Eggs
description: Creamy potato and spinach mash topped with crispy fried eggs. A meat-free weeknight favourite.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Soften the onion in butter, add the spinach and let it wilt. Chop roughly.
Mash the potatoes with milk and butter, fold in the spinach and season with nutmeg.
Fry the eggs and serve two per plate on the stoemp.

name: Ghent Chicken Waterzooi
description: Velvety chicken and vegetable stew from Ghent, finished with cream and egg yolk.
steps: Soften leek, carrot, celery and onion in butter for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, stock cube and 1 litre of water. Simmer for 25 minutes. Add the potatoes and cook 15 minutes more.
Whisk the cream with the egg yolks, stir in a ladle of hot broth, then return to the pan off the heat. Do not boil again.
Season and scatter with parsley. Serve in deep plates.

name: Moules-Frites
description: Mussels steamed with celery, onion and white wine, served with crispy fries.
steps: Clean the mussels and discard any that are broken or stay open when tapped.
Bake the fries according to the packet.
Soften onion and celery in butter in a large pot, add the mussels and wine, cover and steam over high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, shaking the pot.
Add parsley and pepper, toss, and serve immediately with fries and mayonnaise.

name: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
description: Balletjes in tomatensaus: tender meatballs simmered in a rich tomato sauce. Great with fries or bread.
steps: Mix the mince with egg, breadcrumbs, half the onion, salt and pepper. Roll into 16 balls and brown in olive oil.
Soften the remaining onion and the garlic, add tomato paste, tomatoes, thyme and bay leaf.
Add the meatballs and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Serve with fries or crusty bread.

name: Liège Salad
description: Luikse salade: warm salad of green beans and potatoes with crispy bacon and a vinegar-onion dressing.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins; peel and slice. Cook the beans until just tender.
Fry the bacon until crisp. Add the shallots for 2 minutes, then deglaze with the vinegar.
Toss the warm potatoes and beans with the bacon and dressing. Season and finish with parsley.

name: Hutsepot
description: Hearty Flemish winter hotpot of pork, sausages and root vegetables.
steps: Brown the beef and bacon in a large pot. Add the onions, bay leaves, thyme, stock cube and 1.5 litres of water. Simmer for 1 hour.
Add carrots, parsnips, celeriac and leeks; simmer 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes, cabbage and sausages and cook another 30 minutes.
Season and serve the meat and vegetables with a little broth and mustard.

name: Rabbit with Prunes
description: Konijn met pruimen: rabbit braised in dark beer with prunes and thyme.
steps: Season and flour the rabbit and brown it in butter. Remove, then soften the onions in the same pan.
Return the rabbit, add beer, apple syrup, thyme and bay. Cover and braise gently for 60 minutes.
Add the prunes and cook 30 minutes more. Meanwhile boil the potatoes.
Season the sauce and serve with the potatoes.

name: Tomato with Grey Shrimp
description: Tomaat-garnaal: hollowed tomatoes filled with North Sea grey shrimp in mayonnaise.
steps: Cut a lid from each tomato and scoop out the seeds. Season the inside and turn upside down to drain.
Mix the shrimp with mayonnaise, a squeeze of lemon and chives.
Fill the tomatoes, replace the lids and serve on lettuce leaves with fresh bread.

name: Croque Monsieur
description: Toasted ham and cheese sandwich, the café classic.
steps: Butter the outside of each slice of bread.
Assemble with cheese, ham and cheese between the unbuttered sides.
Toast in a sandwich maker or pan for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and melted. Serve with ketchup.

name: Belgian Pancakes
description: Thin pannenkoeken with brown sugar, the Sunday afternoon classic.
steps: Whisk flour, salt and vanilla sugar with the eggs and half of the milk to a smooth batter. Whisk in the rest of the milk and the melted butter.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Cook thin pancakes in a hot buttered pan, about 1 minute per side.
Serve with brown sugar, jam or chocolate spread.

name: Brussels Waffles
description: Light, crisp yeasted waffles dusted with sugar.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm milk. Mix the flour, salt and vanilla sugar, then whisk in the milk, egg yolks, butter and sparkling water.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and fold into the batter. Leave to rise for 1 hour.
Bake in a hot greased waffle iron until golden and crisp. Dust with sugar.

name: Fish Pot with Leek
description: Vispannetje: white fish, shrimp and leek in a creamy sauce under a crust of mashed potato.
steps: Boil the potatoes and mash with milk and a knob of butter.
Soften the leek in butter, stir in the flour, then add 400 ml water and the stock cube. Simmer until thickened and add the cream.
Add the fish and poach for 4 minutes. Stir in the shrimp and dill.
Spoon into an oven dish, cover with mash and cheese and grill at 220 °C for 10 to 15 minutes.

name: Brussels Sprouts with Bacon and Mash
description: Pan-fried sprouts with bacon and nutmeg, served with creamy mashed potatoes.
steps: Trim the sprouts and blanch for 5 minutes. Drain.
Boil and mash the potatoes with milk, butter and nutmeg.
Fry the bacon and onion until golden, add the sprouts and fry until lightly caramelised. Season and serve with the mash.

name: Flemish-Style Asparagus
description: White asparagus with egg-butter sauce, parsley and new potatoes. Spring only.
steps: Peel the asparagus and cook in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Boil the potatoes.
Hard-boil the eggs, peel and mash them with a fork.
Melt the butter, stir in the egg, parsley, a squeeze of lemon and nutmeg.
Serve the asparagus with the potatoes and spoon over the egg butter.

name: Red Cabbage with Apples
description: Sweet-sour braised red cabbage with apples and cinnamon. Freezes perfectly.
steps: Soften the onion in butter, add the cabbage, apples, sugar, vinegar, cinnamon and bay leaves with a splash of water.
Cover and braise gently for 1 hour, stirring now and then.
Season to taste. Serve with pork, game or sausages.

name: Belgian Rice Pudding
description: Rijstpap: creamy saffron-free rice pudding cooked slowly in milk.
steps: Bring the milk to the boil with the salt. Add the rice and simmer very gently for 45 minutes, stirring regularly.
Stir in sugar and vanilla sugar. The pudding thickens as it cools.
Serve warm or cold with a sprinkle of brown sugar.

name: Pumpkin Soup
description: Smooth autumn soup of pumpkin, carrot and ginger.
steps: Soften the onion and ginger in olive oil.
Add pumpkin, carrots, stock cubes and 1.2 litres of water. Simmer for 25 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season.

name: Tomato Soup with Meatballs
description: Tomatensoep met balletjes: the Belgian family soup, with tiny meatballs.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in olive oil. Add fresh and canned tomatoes, tomato paste, stock cubes and 1.2 litres water. Simmer 25 minutes.
Mix the mince with egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and roll into marble-sized balls.
Blend the soup with the basil, bring back to a simmer and poach the meatballs for 8 minutes.

name: Vegetable Soup
description: Groentesoep: everyday clear soup full of vegetables. Makes a big pot.
steps: Soften the onion and leek in olive oil.
Add all other vegetables, stock cubes and 2 litres of water. Simmer 25 minutes.
Season, add parsley and serve as is or partly blended.

name: Endive Stoemp with Pork Chops
description: Mashed potatoes with raw shredded endive, served with pan-fried pork chops.
steps: Boil the potatoes and mash with warm milk, butter and nutmeg.
Fry the bacon until crisp and fold into the mash together with the raw endive.
Season the pork chops and fry 4 to 5 minutes per side. Serve with the stoemp.

name: Celeriac Soup
description: Velvety celeriac and potato soup with a hint of nutmeg.
steps: Soften the leek in butter. Add celeriac, potato, stock cubes and 1.2 litres water and simmer 25 minutes.
Blend smooth, add cream and nutmeg and season. Garnish with chives.
